title: Design URL-driven search with safe caching and indexing lag
businessContext: Each keystroke requests a full server page, mixes tenant results in one cache key and loses filters on navigation.
problemStatement: Design the system for 10 million documents; p95 search under 600 ms; index lag up to 30 seconds. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Communicate stale index semantics and authorization.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 10 million documents; p95 search under 600 ms; index lag up to 30 seconds
functional: Communicate stale index semantics and authorization.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Keep draft input separate from committed URL query state, debounce navigation deliberately and preserve unrelated filters.

A deleted or newly restricted document may remain in the index. Enforce result visibility at a trusted boundary and define removal/permission propagation bounds, rather than assuming eventual indexing lag is acceptable for private data.
alternativeApproaches: It changes bundle and hydration cost, not search correctness. Use server-owned search data and small client interactions, then measure rendering cost and pagination/virtualization needs independently.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Race old/new queries and confirm late results cannot overwrite the current query.
Warm one tenant’s query then repeat it from another.
Delete or revoke indexed content and measure the visibility boundary.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
